headline: Thanksgiving's major coastal storm brings its strongest winds, heaviest rain and worst coastal flooding to New York City this evening, then conditions ease after midnight into a milder, showery Friday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A storm tracking north through the Mid-Atlantic, squeezed against unusually strong high pressure over the Northeast, brings heavy rain and high winds to New York City through about midnight, with the strongest winds and heaviest rain arriving together this evening and even a rumble of thunder possible. Northeast to east winds gust about 45 to 60 mph in the city and along the coast, with a few higher gusts possible, until around 10 PM before easing as a warm front moves in; a High Wind Warning covers the city, Long Island and the Hudson County/Newark-area waterfront until 1 AM Friday, and a Wind Advisory covers areas north and west of the city and inland Connecticut, now also ending at 1 AM. Rain totals of 1 to 2 inches are expected, locally up to 3 inches, but the storm moves quickly and rain should not exceed an inch an hour, so flooding should mostly be minor street and poor-drainage flooding with only a low chance of flash flooding. Temperatures climb into the 50s overnight behind the warm front, with some fog possible as winds briefly calm, then south winds pick back up.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday stays cloudy with a chance of showers as the storm's upper-level low passes to the northwest, with the best chances north and west of the city. Highs reach the mid to upper 50s, though some guidance runs cooler given the clouds and showers, and south-southwest winds gust 25 to 30 mph, turning west after midnight. Saturday looks dry, with west winds gusting about 25 to 30 mph that ease Saturday night.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Sunday looks dry, then showers are likely after midnight Sunday night as a front arrives. A chance of showers lingers Monday morning, with southwest winds gusting about 25 to 30 mph turning west in the afternoon and northwest Monday night. Tuesday looks dry; the discussion gives no temperature details for Sunday through Tuesday.

coast: Storm-force east-northeast winds through the first half of tonight are driving a 3 to 4 foot storm surge, making widespread moderate to major coastal flooding likely at this evening's high tide, and forecast water levels have edged up a bit; Coastal Flood Warnings run until 6 AM Friday everywhere except southeastern Connecticut. Significant impacts are expected around Peconic Bay, with surge funneling toward the Peconic River, and along the western Long Island Sound shoreline where high water combines with large waves, while surge up the Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic rivers brings minor to moderate flooding; heavy rain at high tide could worsen coastal street flooding. For Friday morning's high tide, winds turn southwest and widespread minor flooding is likely, locally moderate in the back bays of western Long Island's south shore, with Coastal Flood Advisories in effect Friday morning into early afternoon for all coastal areas (the earlier watch for the south shore of Long Island is now an advisory). Ocean beaches see 8 to 12 foot breaking waves with widespread beach flooding, dune erosion and possible localized overwashes flooding roads and buildings behind the dunes, while western Long Island Sound and the Twin Forks see 3 to 6 foot breakers with dune erosion, splashover and possible isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures. On the water, a Storm Warning runs until 1 AM Friday, with ocean seas near 20 feet this evening, waves near 10 feet on the Sound and at the New York Harbor entrance, and gusts often 60 to 70 mph this evening; a southwest gale is likely on the ocean Friday, easing to small-craft-advisory levels Saturday and likely below that Sunday, with southwest to west gales possible on the ocean again Monday.
watch_for: This evening's high tide, arriving with the heaviest rain and strongest winds
Exact timing of the peak winds and heaviest rain, which could be off by a few hours
Possible fog overnight as winds calm behind the warm front
confidence: Forecasters are confident in tonight's high winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding though timing could shift by a few hours, have low confidence in overnight fog, and note Friday could turn out cooler than forecast.
